sentences.text: ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024

Court No. - 86
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 5055 of 2023
Revisionist :- Rajeev Parashar

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Revisionist :- Jai Prakash Prasad,Rakesh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Ankur Singh Kushwaha,G.A.
Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.
1.

Instant Criminal Revision has been preferred against impugned order dated 07.05.2024 passed by learned Civil Judge (JD)/FTC-I, Muzaffar Nagar in Case Crime No.1603 of 2015 arising out of Case Crime No.16 of 2011, under Sections 420, 504, 506, 386 IPC, P.S. Mahila Thana, Districts Muzaffar Nagar.
By the impugned order, learned trial court has dismissed the application filed by the revisionist/accused wherein prayer for discharged has been made.

2. However, during pendency of present revision before this Court it appears that charges have been framed on 01.03.2004 and an amendment in prayer clause of Revision Memo has been incorporated by the revisionist by seeking permission from this Court and a prayer has already been added therein for quashing the charges framed against the revisionist under said sections.
3.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionist, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that revisionist has taken a suitable plea in discharge application, no charge under Section 386 IPC is made out, even if the allegations in the FIR are taken on face value, as there is no accusation or allegation that any money has passed on pursuant to alleged extortion consequent upon threat put-forth by the accused on defacto complainant.
The case does not goes beyond the extent of Section 406 IPC.
Even no case under Sections 504 & 506 IPC is made out for want of specific averments as required for meted out said charges.

However, learned trial court consider the grounds taken in discharge application and dismissed the discharge application in mechanical manner after citing certain judicial pronouncement without any expression of opinion as to how these are applicable on facts and circumstances in hand.
5. Per contra
learned

counsel for the respondent No.2 raised a preliminary objection and submitted that not only charges have been framed in the case against the revisionist, but the case is fixed for prosecution evidence and two witnesses have already been examined from on behalf of prosecution.
Therefore, present revision is not maintainable.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 placed reliance on a recent and reported judgment of this Court in Criminal Revision No.2183 of 2021 connected with application under Section 482 No.13664 of 2021 Ravindra Pratap Pratap Shahi @ Pappu Shahi Vs. State of U.P. and another wherein a co-ordinate Bench of this Court on similar state of things held in paragraph Nos.32, 33 and 34 are as follows:-
"32.

entities.text: Ravindra Pratap Pratap Shahi @ Pappu Shahi Vs. State of U.P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, discharge claimed by applicant/revisionist has been refused by Court below, vide order dated 02.09.2021.
Criminal Revision preferred by applicant/revisionist cannot be considered now as charges have already been framed.

Thus by necessary implication, this Court now cannot examine the veracity of the framing of charge order dated 04.09.2021.
33.

Apart from above, when framing of charge order is examined in the light of ambit and scope of Section 228 Cr. P. C. as defined by Apex Court in aforementioned judgement, this Court is of considered opinion that at this stage, it cannot be said that no offence under Section 306 IPC is made out against applicant/revisionist.

Arguments raised on behalf of applicant/revisionist, the submissions urged by learned A.G.A. and Mr. S.N. Singh, learned counsel representing opposite party 2 will all have to be considered to decide the correctness of order dated 04.09.2021.

This exercise will itself amount to mini trial, which is not permissible, while deciding the correctness of an order passed in terms of Section 228 Cr. P. C.
34.
For the facts and reasons noted above, this Court does not find any good ground to interfere.

As a result, Criminal Misc. Application as well as Criminal Revision filed by applicant/revisionist are liable to be dismissed."
7.

Taking into consideration the judgment cited by leaned counsel for the respondent No.2, in support of his contention regarding maintainability of present revision in change circumstances, I Rajeev Parashar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56333827/
2 find force in submissions of learned cousnel and the revision is found not maintainable, as it deserves to be dismissed, without going into the merits of the grounds taken in present revision as the trial is progressing in the case.
8. Revision is dismissed.
